A crime author came across Tamara’s post and offered to help her access the Rochester Police Department’s case documents. Tamara says what she read forever altered her understanding of her mother’s death. A life cut short Dateline obtained the same report from the Rochester Police Department. The initial entry states that at 11:24 p.m. on May 23, 1975, Rochester Police dispatch received a phone call reporting “family trouble” at a home on Kron Street in the city’s 19th Ward. According to the report, Officer Paul Camping was dispatched to the scene, where he knocked repeatedly on the front door to no response. Finding the house dark and quiet, he left. The report notes that an hour later, at 12:33 a.m., police received another call: this time from Snookie’s husband, Lewis Evans. Officer Camping returned to the scene and found Lewis “standing outside in an incoherent condition.” He told the responding officer he had just returned home from work at Rochester Products, a local manufacturing company, when he discovered his wife. Snookie was found dead in the living room, “lying face down with her ankles tied together with a white cloth,” according to the police report. The report also notes that a kitchen knife and a cast-iron frying pan were strewn on the floor, and the living room TV was on. Although the home appeared ransacked, there were no signs of forced entry. Lewis told police at the time that $1,100 in cash was missing from a metal box in the living room. The medical examiner’s office determined Snookie had multiple stab wounds and noted she had been nearly decapitated. The estimated time of death was placed between 11:30 p.m. and 12:30 a.m. Tamara was just 3 months old when her mother was killed. Daryl was only 2. Their half brothers on their father’s side were 4 and 6. They were all found inside the home, unharmed. Although Tamara and Daryl have no memories of their mother, the descriptions they’ve heard over the years are consistent: a sweet, devoted parent. Growing up, Snookie was close to her sister, Ellen Evans. “We walked to school together, eat lunch together. We just did everything together,” Ellen told Dateline. “She was the one who kept me grounded. She was the calm.” Gina Alves, married to Snookie and Ellen’s cousin at the time, fondly remembers her friendship with Snookie. “Norris is just so sweet. I really loved her,” Gina told Dateline. “Through her pregnancy, with — what they call him, Tiger — Daryl, he was the cutest baby, and then she got pregnant with her daughter. She was just so excited, you know, ‘Oh, I got a girl! I got a girl!’” Gina says Snookie called her the night she died and asked if she wanted to play cards. “I’ll never forget that I was watching [The] Andy Griffith [Show] and she said, ‘Well, why don’t you guys come over?’” Gina said, choking up. She didn’t end up going. “So then, you know, that happened to her, and I always wonder, maybe if we would’ve went over there, maybe that wouldn’t have happened to her.” Ellen told Dateline she remembers the exact moment their father told her what happened to Snookie. “I slapped him. I slapped him so hard and told him, ‘You’re lying. You’re lying,’” she said. The investigation The Rochester Police Department launched an investigation into Snookie’s killing that would span years, chasing lead after lead. According to their report, Rochester police first looked into those with histories of violent burglaries in the area. They investigated at least 10 people who fit the description, checking fingerprints, administering polygraph exams and checking alibis without making an arrest. Ellen Evans told Dateline the family had its suspicions. She had introduced Snookie to Lewis Evans, the brother of Ellen’s estranged husband. “At first they were happy together,” she said. But as the relationship evolved, Ellen says it became clear to her that Snookie had grown scared of Lewis. “And all of a sudden, he was jealous, and he didn’t want us to hang out together.” Police also spoke with Ellen and Snookie’s cousin Ronald Purdue, who said he received a call from Snookie the morning of her death. “The victim stated to him that she was very depressed and she wanted to get away from her husband, as she was no longer in love with him,” the police report states. “She went on to say that because she was afraid of her husband she was afraid to leave.” Two days after his interview, Ronald called the Rochester Police Department and said he had additional information. A sergeant was dispatched to his residence to interview Ronald and his wife. According to the police report, Ronald said Snookie’s grandmother had asked young Daryl if he knew who hurt his mommy, to which the toddler responded, “Daddy hurt Mommy.” The couple told investigators they didn’t believe any money had been stolen from the house, because Lewis “never left that kind of money around the house for any reason,” according to the police report. They also stated that given the trouble in the relationship, if Snookie “knew the money was in the house she would have taken it and left him.” At the time of Snookie’s death, Lewis was also involved with a woman named Gail Bloodsaw, according to the police report. When she spoke to police in 1975, she told them she had been going out with Lewis since November 1974. The report notes that Gail said Lewis called her three times between 6 p.m. and 10 p.m. on the evening of May 23, 1975. She assumed he was at work because of the machine noise in the background. She also told them he had visited her after work at approximately 12:30 a.m. — around the same time Lewis had placed a call from Kron Street. The police report includes notes from a later interview with Gail Bloodsaw, as well, who the report now described as Lewis’ common-law wife. When she was re-interviewed in 1977, Gail told reporting officers that she had lied to police in her earlier interview and that Lewis had not visited her that night. As she was being interviewed at the station, Lewis arrived and appeared to be “very upset,” according to the report. “Mr. Evans was advised that the Police were just trying to find out who killed his wife & Mr. Evans stated that he did not want the police to do anything regarding the case,” the report states. While at the station, investigators asked Lewis “if he would be willing to speak with Inv. officers about the incident & he refused,” the report notes. During that same 1977 interview, according to the police report, Gail was asked if she had ever forged Snookie’s name on documents, and she replied that she had forged Snookie’s signature during a hospital visit in March 1975 in order to use her health insurance. The police report states that a handwriting expert from the Physical Crimes Unit then examined samples and determined that Gail had also forged Snookie’s signature on a life insurance policy Lewis took out on himself on May 15, 1975, eight days before Snookie’s death. When informed of the finding, Gail said “she believes she may have forged Norris[’s] name to the policy but does not recall doing so,” the report stated. According to the Rochester Police Department, there was not “sufficient evidence to say with certainty the document was forged.” Dateline reached out by phone to Gail Bloodsaw Evans for comment on the events of 1975. She responded, “We have no input on that,” and ended the call. John Hancock Mutual Life Insurance Company provided investigators with an explanation of two life insurance policies involving Snookie. Dateline obtained a copy of the letter from the Rochester Police Department. The first policy was one Snookie had taken out on herself in 1971. In 1973, she changed the policy to update it to her married name and changed the beneficiary from her mother to her husband, according to the letter. The second policy was the one Lewis took out on himself on May 15, 1975. The letter stated that policy included “Family Insurance” of $1,250 on each of his children, and $1,000 on his wife. The policy also included “Decreasing Term Insurance on the Insured’s wife in the amount of $10,000 for 25 years.” John Hancock noted Lewis Evans was the beneficiary in the event of the death of his wife. The company, “knowing of no reason why payment should not be made in accordance with the Beneficiary Designation of record, paid the policy proceeds to Mr. Evans,” the letter states. In one of his interviews with police in the days following Snookie’s death, Lewis “denied killing his wife and stated that he spent the entire night, from 3:30PM. to 12:08 AM at work (Roch. Prod.)” According to the report, Lewis’ timecard from Rochester Products shows he clocked in at 3:54 p.m. The report also shows that investigators interviewed Lewis’ supervisor who said he relieved Lewis twice on the night of May 23, 1975: during a meal break at 7:55 until about 8:30 or 8:40 p.m., and again from about 10 to 10:30 p.m. Co-workers interviewed by police reported seeing him playing cards at the plant after 11 p.m. The report notes that Lewis’ timecard shows he clocked out at 12:08 a.m. After speaking with witnesses at the plant, “we cannot implicate Evans as being involved in his wifes [sic] death as we can find no-one to say he left the building,” the police report states. Rochester police interviewed two of Lewis’ male relatives: his half brother Leroy Barnes and their cousin Jessie Martin. The three were very close, Ellen said. Neighbors frequently saw them outside Lewis’ home at 5 Kron Street, according to the case report. Leroy and Jessie were at Lewis’ house the afternoon of May 23, 1975, helping him paint his car, they told police at the time. Jessie told police he walked home when Lewis left for work and stayed there the rest of the night. Leroy said he went to the park until about 7:30 p.m., after which he went to a series of bars and nightclubs, which several alibi witnesses confirmed. Both Leroy and Jessie refused polygraph tests, according to the report. The file also details that a neighbor visited Snookie from about 7:15 to 7:30 p.m., around the same time she called Gina to ask if she wanted to play cards. A different neighbor walked by around 7:45 p.m. and saw Snookie sitting on her front porch. That was the last time anyone reported seeing Snookie alive. Two other neighbors were on a nearby porch from about 11:30 p.m. to 12:15 a.m. Other than Officer Camping’s first arrival, neither of them saw anything out of the ordinary at 5 Kron Street, the police report says. Ellen Evans and Gina Alves told Dateline the family was convinced of Lewis’ involvement. “I don’t know if he physically did it, or there was something that was going on that he had a part in,” Gina said. “But the whole family just felt that.” Decades cold When Snookie’s children, Tamara and Daryl, read the contents of the police report in 2021, they saw their mother’s death in a new light. The siblings told Dateline they had remained in their father’s care, and despite rumors in the extended family, were largely kept in the dark about their mom’s case. “I only knew that she was killed, and that it was someone she knew, because there were no signs of forced entry,” Tamara told Dateline. Both Tamara and Daryl can only remember a handful of times Snookie was mentioned as they were growing up. They also say their father kept them away from their mother’s side of the family. “I rarely heard him speak about her personality as a mother, how she nurtured us, cared for us, or what she was like in daily family life after Daryl and I were born,” Tamara wrote in a follow-up email to Dateline. “I wish I had more of those kinds of memories and stories.” “You hear tidbits of information growing up,” Daryl said. But after reading the police report, he says, everything came together. “I really saw a clear picture of who, what, when, why, where.” Tamara and Daryl told Dateline that after reading through the police report, they called on the Rochester Police Department to look into the case again. It was assigned to Investigator Seth Carr of the Major Crimes Unit in 2022. “The truth is, I kid you not, I walked into Capt. Umbrino’s office, and I told him this case should be on Dateline,” Investigator Carr said. “The kids being involved in trying to figure out what happened to their mother, even with the understanding that that may result in their father being implicated. You know, it’s an interesting dynamic.” Over the next couple of years, Investigator Carr conducted several follow-up interviews, including with Lewis Evans. According to Carr, Lewis gave the same response to every question: “I have nothing to add and nothing to take away.” Carr says he’s considered whether the timing of the 11:24 p.m. anonymous phone call to police could have been intended to steer investigators toward a period when certain people in the case had stronger alibis. “There’s certainly a possibility that that’s not a coincidence,” he said. “That this phone call is made and their alibis are strongest at that time, because maybe the goal is to make the police department believe that the crime occurred at that time.” Considering a time-of-death window wider than the estimated 11:30 p.m. to 12:30 a.m. period opens up new potential scenarios, he added. No one has been charged in connection with the case, and no suspects have been named in Snookie’s death. “It’s fair to say Jessie Martin, Lewis Ev[a]ns and Leroy Barnes (deceased) all remain persons of interest in the case,” Carr said in a follow-up email. When Dateline contacted Lewis Evans about Snookie’s case, he responded: “I don’t know anything about that. Have a good day.” He has declined further calls. Dateline also attempted to contact Jessie Martin for comment. His wife answered the phone and said he was unavailable to speak with us. Dateline asked her to pass along our message, but we have not heard back. The way forward Regarding the case status, Rochester Police Capt. Frank Umbrino and Investigator Carr agree: someone must come forward for the case to progress. Although several forensic samples were pulled from the crime scene — including hair, blood, and fabric — they were not preserved properly to undergo modern forensic testing, Capt. Umbrino told Dateline. “We would need somebody that has direct knowledge of who did the murder, who orchestrated the murder, and they would have to be willing to get up on a stand and testify,” he said. “That’s the only thing that’s going to push this case forward.” Ellen Evans has lived 51 years without her sister. The grief never left. “For years I’d cry,” Ellen said. “Her young life was cut short. She had so much to give.” Tamara Sinclair has lived all but three months of her life without her mother. She says she wakes up every day and thinks about her. She wishes she could call her and tell her about her own children. When asked what justice might look like, Tamara wasn’t sure. “I would have accepted accountability and an apology,” she said. “If the truth could just come out,” Gina Alves said. “I just think that one way or another, you just can’t get away with things.” There is one positive outcome to the siblings’ search for answers. Back in 2021, Gina stumbled across Tamara’s Facebook post asking if anyone knew what happened to her mother. She and Snookie’s cousin separated decades ago, and she hadn’t seen Tamara and Daryl since they were children. After seeing the post, they reconnected. “All these years I’m wondering what happened to Snookie’s babies,” she said. “And then I actually got to see Tiger and I got to see Tammy, and all I could do was just hug them and hug them and hug them.” “I always felt that Snookie was their guardian angel,” she said. “She watched over her babies all these years.” If you have information about the Norris “Snookie” Evans case, you can submit a tip to Rochester NY Unsolved or call the Rochester Police Department’s Major Crimes Unit at 585-428-7157. To leave a tip anonymously, please call Rochester Area Crime Stoppers at 585-423-9300. If you have a story to share with Dateline, please submit it here.

articles.title: Teams working to avoid 'impactful' wildfires in South West
articles.summary: Rangers and marshals are working to educate people about fire risks on Dartmoor after a dry summer.
articles.body:
People have been urged to avoid starting fires in national parks and moorland due to the dry conditions.

Marshals at Dartmoor National Park in Devon have been on patrol advising people about the risks while firebreaks have also been built to help stop flames spreading.

Deputy head ranger Ella Briens said fires were not allowed in the park as wildfires at this time of year could have a big impact on the surroundings.

Cornwall Fire and Rescue Service said people should not to use disposable barbecues while bonfires, campfires and fireworks should all be avoided.

Briens said the team on Dartmoor had to move people in tents in areas closed to camping and found the remains of barbecues which had scorched the parched grass around them.

She added other fire hazards include discarded bottles.

"We just don't want glass lying around, it's going to be a source of ignition if the sun shines through that," Briens said.

In May 2025, a large wildfire on Dartmoor destroyed about 1,230 acres (5 sq km) of land.

Ranger Luke Engel, speaking to the BBC after spotting another discarded barbecue and abandoned tent at Cadover Bridge, said: "All it takes sometimes is a bit of wood, a spark just spreading to another bit, and when the ground's really dry it can spread anywhere."

Dartmoor fire marshal Lewis Edwards said people sometimes needed "a gentle nudge in the right direction" to make sure they are being safe and using the right areas for camping.

He said because of the heatwaves, marshals had to "step in and really clamp down on people having open fires, disposable barbecues and things like that".

Visitors were more aware of the risk, he said, with the extra signage on the moor and the alert sent by the government to mobile phones.

"We just need to keep promoting it," he added.

The Dartmoor team's warnings came after Devon's assistant chief fire officer Darren Mclatchey said most wildfire incidents were directly impacted by humans from "careless disposal, accidental and deliberate fires".

Fire service officials in Devon and Cornwall said crews had dealt with hundreds of fires in the open during the summer.

Mclatchey said the government's temporary ban on the sale of disposable barbecues "does help" and added they "aren't necessarily a dangerous item" if they were disposed of "carefully and considerately".

He said the service was planning for the pressures of coping with climate change.

"We absolutely recognise that there's a long-term if not permanent change in climate," he said.

"Part of our planning and preparation is to look at how we will respond to wide-scale incidents, how we prepare for it and how we invest into it."

Mclatchey added: "We have the resources that we need, we will plan for the future as best as possible.

"But I think ultimately it's going to be very difficult for anybody to plan to know exactly what the future will hold we just have to respond to it and plan to it as best we can."

He said they were looking at the risks and "invest into the right area so we're able to respond appropriately".

The service was planning its response to El Niño which could bring powerful winds and "what that might look at for our region".

Cornwall Fire and Rescue Service said crews had received a "high volume" of 999 calls since Friday and would be unable to attend reports of neighbours using barbecues, fire pits or bonfires in private gardens unless there was an immediate threat to life, property or the environment.

Firefighters said it would discourage people from doing open burning as the conditions meant even small fires could "spread rapidly and become difficult to control".

"With Cornwall currently in official drought conditions and a hosepipe ban in force, Cornwall Fire Service is also urging residents, landowners and visitors to avoid carrying out any controlled burns," a fire service spokesperson said.

"Ground and vegetation conditions across the county remain exceptionally dry, significantly increasing the likelihood of fire spread.

"Without immediate and effective means of extinguishment, a controlled burn can quickly escalate, endangering people, property, wildlife and the natural environment."

articles.title: Quote of the day by Plato: "Wonder is the feeling of a philosopher, and philosophy begins inâ¦"
articles.summary: Europe News: Two people can hit the exact same confusing, unresolved question and respond in completely different ways. One feels the confusion purely as discomfor.
articles.body: Two people can hit the exact same confusing, unresolved question and respond in completely different ways. One feels the confusion purely as discomfort, something to be resolved as quickly as possible by picking whichever answer sounds most reasonable and then moving on without looking back. The other feels that same confusion as something closer to fascination, a genuine puzzle worth sitting inside rather than rushing past on the way to relief. Plato put this second reaction at the very root of philosophical thinking itself. In the dialogue Theaetetus, written around 369 BC, he has Socrates respond to a young mathematician's confusion, his dizziness at realizing he can't fully explain what knowledge actually is, not with reassurance meant to settle the confusion down, but with something closer to approval, telling him that this exact feeling, wonder, is the mark of someone doing philosophy correctly, rather than a sign that something in the conversation has gone wrong. This ancient insight remains remarkably relevant today, reminding us that genuine intellectual growth requires embracing uncertainty rather than rushing toward comfortable, premature conclusions.Quote of the day by Plato: "Wonder is the feeling of a philosopher, and philosophy begins in wonder."Written inside a dialogue about the nature of knowledge itselfWhat gives this line extra weight is the specific conversation it comes from. Theaetetus is structured as an attempt to define knowledge, and across the dialogue, every proposed definition that Theaetetus offers- knowledge as perception, knowledge as true belief, knowledge as true belief with an account- gets carefully taken apart by Socrates, leaving Theaetetus increasingly disoriented rather than increasingly certain. It's at that exact point of disorientation, when the ground seems to be giving way under a concept everyone assumes they already understand, that Socrates names wonder as the beginning of the whole enterprise rather than its failure.That framing reflects something central to how Plato understood philosophy's origins more broadly. His own philosophical life began in the shadow of his teacher Socrates's trial and execution in 399 BC, an event that left Plato deeply unsettled about the relationship between conventional certainty and actual truth, and that pushed him to found the Academy in Athens, widely regarded as one of the first institutions of higher learning in the Western world, built specifically around the same relentless, unsettled questioning that runs through his dialogues. Wonder, for Plato, was never a symptom to be cured on the way to an answer. It was the entry point into philosophy itself, the state a serious thinker was supposed to return to again and again rather than escape as quickly as possible.A simple way to actually use this ideaThe useful move here is treating confusion about something fundamental as a signal worth paying attention to rather than a problem to be resolved as fast as possible. Modern habits often push in the opposite direction, toward quick answers, tidy explanations, and a general discomfort with sitting inside genuine uncertainty for very long. Plato's version of philosophy asks for the opposite instinct: when a familiar concept, knowledge, fairness, happiness, suddenly stops making obvious sense under close examination, that disorientation is not evidence the thinking has gone wrong. It's evidence the thinking has finally reached something worth examining.A fair test, the next time an ordinary assumption suddenly seems less obvious than it did a moment ago, is to ask whether the confusion is worth staying with a little longer rather than being smoothed over immediately. That question won't resolve every genuine puzzle. It usually keeps a real question from being replaced too quickly by a convenient, half-examined answer.Other famous quotes by Plato"The beginning is the most important part of the work." "Ignorance, the root and stem of all evil." "Human behavior flows from three main sources: desire, emotion, and knowledge."Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Zolani Tete: Four arrested over boxing champion's murder in South Africa
articles.summary: One of the suspects is due in court on Monday to be charged with murder and attempted murder.
articles.body:
Four people have been arrested in South Africa in connection with the murder of boxing champion Zolani Tete, who was shot dead outside his home on Friday.

Tete, 38, was gunned down in what has been described as an ambush in Mdantsane, Eastern Cape. A young woman who was with him was also shot and is in hospital.

One of the men being held, a 22-year-old who was arrested on Saturday, will make an initial appearance in court on Monday, and faces murder and attempted murder charges.

Tete held the WBO bantamweight title from 2017 to 2019, as well as the IBF super-flyweight title in 2014. He was later given a four-year ban, which lapsed in July this year.

The remaining suspects, who were arrested on Sunday, are due in court on Tuesday. Two have been charged with unlawful possession of firearms and ammunition. It is unclear whether they will also be charged with murder and attempted murder.

Tete was in his car waiting for the gate to his house to open when two armed suspects in balaclavas emerged from a vehicle and fired "multiple shots" at him and a 27‑year‑old female passenger, according to officials.

The motive behind the attack is unclear.

Tributes have been pouring in for the two-time world champion since his death. South Africa's Sports Minister Gayton McKenzie said: "South Africa has lost one of the finest fighters it has ever produced."

Former Sports Minister Fikile Mbalula also paid tribute to Tete, lamenting the loss of a "a great South African who has made an immense contribution in the sport of boxing".

Tete beat Liverpool's Paul Butler in 2015 in one of the eight times he fought in the United Kingdom.

He also holds a Guinness World Record for the fastest knockout in a title fight, ending his match with Siboniso Gonya inside 11 seconds in 2017.

Tete last fought in July 2022, beating Briton Jason Cunningham by knockout In London, but it was later ruled a no-contest after he failed a drugs test.

He tested positive for anabolic steroid stanozolol and was given a ban by the UK Anti-Doping Agency.

paragraphs: Four people have been arrested in South Africa in connection with the murder of boxing champion Zolani Tete, who was shot dead outside his home on Friday.
Tete, 38, was gunned down in what has been described as an ambush in Mdantsane, Eastern Cape. A young woman who was with him was also shot and is in hospital.
One of the men being held, a 22-year-old who was arrested on Saturday, will make an initial appearance in court on Monday, and faces murder and attempted murder charges.
Tete held the WBO bantamweight title from 2017 to 2019, as well as the IBF super-flyweight title in 2014. He was later given a four-year ban, which lapsed in July this year.

The remaining suspects, who were arrested on Sunday, are due in court on Tuesday. Two have been charged with unlawful possession of firearms and ammunition. It is unclear whether they will also be charged with murder and attempted murder.

Tete was in his car waiting for the gate to his house to open when two armed suspects in balaclavas emerged from a vehicle and fired "multiple shots" at him and a 27‑year‑old female passenger, according to officials.
The motive behind the attack is unclear.

Tributes have been pouring in for the two-time world champion since his death. South Africa's Sports Minister Gayton McKenzie said: "South Africa has lost one of the finest fighters it has ever produced."
Former Sports Minister Fikile Mbalula also paid tribute to Tete, lamenting the loss of a "a great South African who has made an immense contribution in the sport of boxing".
Tete beat Liverpool's Paul Butler in 2015 in one of the eight times he fought in the United Kingdom.
He also holds a Guinness World Record for the fastest knockout in a title fight, ending his match with Siboniso Gonya inside 11 seconds in 2017.

articles.title: In 1900, JP Morgan bought 117 acres including Maineâs Sand Beach as a wedding gift; his granddaughter later donated about 100 acres to Acadia National Park
articles.summary: US News: In 1900, financier J P Morgan bought 117 acres in Maine, including Sand Beach and Great Head, as a wedding gift for his daughter Louisa. The land is n.
articles.body: In 1900, financier J P Morgan bought 117 acres in Maine, including Sand Beach and Great Head, as a wedding gift for his daughter Louisa. The land is now part of Acadia National Park.The land around Great Head and Sand Beach was connected to Louisa and and her husband Herbert Satterlee for decades before it became a public property. According to National Park Service, the familyâs summer property was commonly known as 'Satterlee field'.The 117 acres purchased by financier J P Morgan included Sand Beach and Great Head. Louisa married Herbert Satterlee in New York City in November 1900. The couple later made the coastal property part of their familyâs summer life.Louisa and Herbert had two daughters, Mabel, born in 1901, and Eleanor, born in 1905. The two girls grew up exploring the landscape around their familyâs property.The story of Satterlee FieldAlthough J P Morgan purchased the land in 1900, the transaction was not formally completed until 1910 because of title issues.Before the property eventually became part of the Satterlee familyâs estate, the family already had a connection with Acadia National Park because large sections of park land bordered Satterlee Field. The Satterlees also allowed park visitors to explore Sand Beach while the land was still associated with the family.The familyâs time at the summer estate came to an end after the deaths of Louisa and Herbert. Louisa died in October 1946, while Herbert died in July 1947.A few months later, the area was hit by the October Fire of 1947. Much of the Satterlee estate was destroyed in the fire. After the fire, the familyâs connection to the land changed. Eleanor and Mabel decided to donate the property so that other people could continue to visit and enjoy the landscape that had been important to their family.How family estate became public landEleanor Morgan Satterlee, Louisa and Herbertâs daughter and J P Morganâs granddaughter, inherited the tract after her parents died. By the late 1940s, Eleanorâs health had also begun to decline.These circumstances, along with the damage caused by the 1947 fire, led Eleanor to donate the land to Acadia National Park in 1949. The donation included the area around Great Head, including Sand Beach.The National Park Service records that Eleanor donated approximately 100 acres to the United States in memory of her mother, Louisa P Satterlee.A bronze plaque near the top of the staircase leading down to Sand Beach marks the donation. It carries the following inscription- âSatterlee Field, of approximately 100 acres, was donated in 1949 by Eleanor Morgan Satterlee to the United States of America in memory of her mother, Louisa P. Satterlee, as part of Acadia National Park.âThe landscape todayThe property includes the sandy beach, reached by a staircase, and the stretch of land known as the Headlands. The National Park Service describes the landscape in terms of a human body, with the coastline forming the 'shoulders' and the projecting land resembling a 'head'.The area can now be explored by visitors through the Great Head Trail. The same combination of beach, forest, mountains and coastline that the Satterlee family knew remains part of the visitor experience at Acadia.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Zambia elections: Courts sealed as election petition deadline looms
articles.summary: Preparations for President Hakainde Hichilema's second inauguration appear to be continuing.
articles.body:
Court premises in the Zambian capital, Lusaka, and elsewhere have been shut as the deadline for filing a petition against the outcome of the recent presidential election approaches.

An unusual police presence has been reported at some courts, which have been taped off to prevent access.

Opposition candidate Brian Mundubile said he would challenge the election result, citing irregularities, after coming second with a 38% share of the vote. Incumbent Hakainde Hichilema won a second term with 60%.

Mundubile is in hiding over alleged threats made against him, amid a post-election period marked by controversy, including the shooting dead of an opposition figure and the arrest of others.

Monday is the last day on which petition against the presidential election result can be filed. Such a petition could potentially affect the inauguration of Hichilema, which is scheduled for 1 September.

On Monday, lawyers who arrived at the courts were being asked to depart.

One lawyer told the BBC that three armed men approached his vehicle, identified themselves, and instructed him to leave the area.

The courts that have been sealed off include the High Court in Lusaka, the Supreme Court, which also houses the Constitutional Court, and several local courts.

It is unclear when the premises will reopen. The BBC has contacted the Zambian police and the judiciary for comment.

Local media cite a directive by a judiciary administrative official telling all staff not to report to work following the closure of courts for "security reasons".

The memo, which has also been shared online by some opposition figures, does not give details of the security situation.

Some commentators have raised concerns over the closure while questioning the independence of the judiciary.

A prominent voice for the opposition, Emmanuel Mwamba, alleged the action was aimed at preventing Mundubile from filing his presidential election petition.

The Law Association of Zambia (LAZ) said it was concerned by the closure of the courts and the presence of heavily armed military personnel around court premises in Lusaka.

It said there was no formal public explanation for the closure nor its expected duration.

Referring to the "unsigned memorandum" from the judiciary addressing staff, it said no further official information had been provided to lawyers and the public.

"The closure of the courts has immediate implications for access to justice, particularly for persons requiring urgent judicial intervention," it said in a statement

It said the timing was "particularly significant in the present electoral context", citing a "seven-day period" in which a person may "petition the Constitutional Court to nullify the election of a President-elect".

Despite the court closure, preparations for Hichilema's inauguration appear to be continuing.

The youth and sport ministry has issued a media invitation for journalists to accompany a cabinet official on an inspection of arrangements at National Heroes Stadium, where the ceremony is expected to take place.

Mundubile last week rejected the presidential election results and said he planned to challenge the outcome through the courts.

He remains in a secure location under the protection of what his campaign describes as an "international human rights body".

He went into hiding after the arrests of opposition figures and the death of former minister Mutotwe Kafwaya during a raid by security officers, in what officials described as an exchange of fire in a security operation in the capital.

The arrests as well as the death of Kafwaya prompted calls from rights groups and the Law Association of Zambia for an independent investigations.

Amnesty International described the Kafwaya's killing as "deeply alarming" and called for prompt, thorough and impartial investigations. The lawyers' association similarly expressed "grave concern" and demanded investigation.

The election day, 13 August, was described by regional and international observers as largely peaceful, but they raised concerns about late electoral reforms, media freedom and access to the media in the run-up to the poll.

The EU observation mission said restrictions on the opposition may have contributed to an "uneven contest".

On vote tallying, the mission described a heavy military presence as intimidating and said it had received reports of attacks on some tallying centres.

It said staff in many centres did not record results on tally sheets as soon as they were announced, and cited weak verification between digital entries and paper records. It added that returning officers frequently paused proceedings while awaiting instructions from headquarters.

The EU mission also called for "maximal transparency" over the poll outcome, noting that the electoral commission did not publish separate polling-station results

articles.title: Firefighters make progress against Reno, Nevada, wildfire that’s destroyed over 30 homes
articles.summary: At least six people — three first responders and three civilians — were injured. Officials said the fire was “human-caused” but didn’t provide details about how they reached that conclusion or whether it was intentionally set or accidental.
articles.body: RENO, Nevada — Crews have started to contain a wildfire in the Sierra Nevada foothills near Reno, Nevada, that destroyed more than 30 homes as it spread perilously close to dense neighborhoods, officials said Monday. Containment reached 27% and there was no new growth of the Hawk Fire, which has held steady at about 23 square miles since it burned out of control on Sunday, authorities said at an afternoon news briefing. “We are making progress,” said U.S. Forest Service District Ranger Matt Zumstein. The number of residents under evacuation orders and warnings was reduced to about 63,000, down from more than 90,000 people when the blaze mushroomed over the weekend. While winds have eased, there’s still concern that gusts could push the flames through dry brush into newly developed neighborhoods in Nevada’s largest city outside of metro Las Vegas. Firefighters are also contending with hot temperatures and low humidity. At least 32 homes have burned and six are damaged, but authorities said those numbers are sure to rise as assessment teams begin to survey the charred areas. Reno Mayor Hillary Schieve said the way the fire spread so quickly at its height had her fearing for the worst. “It lit up these areas like nothing I’ve seen before,” she said Monday. “It took your breath away, in the worst way.” Hawk Fire triggers evacuations and school closures Schools across Washoe County were closed Monday because of the evacuations and to keep roads clear for emergency crews. Nevada’s governor declared a state of emergency in the county and mobilized the National Guard to help with aerial firefighting and protecting evacuated neighborhoods northwest of downtown Reno. At one roadblock, residents expressed frustration Monday that they could not get back into their homes. “There’s no fire here! Why are the National Guard here?” a driver yelled. Washoe County Sheriff Darin Balaam said he understands that some residents are frustrated that they can’t get home, but the danger isn’t over yet. “It just takes that little breeze and one ember,” he said. Wildfires near Reno are blamed on human activity The fire near the California state line began Saturday and exploded in size on Sunday. At least seven people — three first responders and four civilians — have been injured. This is the third large wildfire in the rugged terrain north of Reno in the past two weeks — all caused by human activity, according to fire officials. They haven’t said whether the Hawk Fire was intentionally set or accidental. Much of the area that burned was sagebrush and grass. Reno, home to about 280,000 people, is known for its casinos and as a gateway to nearby Lake Tahoe, North America’s largest alpine lake and a popular vacation destination. It’s also southwest of Nevada’s Black Rock Desert, site of the annual Burning Man festival, which begins next Sunday. Many who travel to Burning Man make Reno a regular stop. Organizers on Monday asked attendees to not take hotel rooms and other resources away from fire evacuees, while being mindful of closures. “Treat our neighbors, first responders, hospitality workers and everyone affected by this emergency with patience and care,” a Burning Man statement said. Fire claims a Reno woman’s home for a second time Videos posted on social media showed the smoldering ruins of homes and cars, with only a scorched basketball hoop still standing. Crystal Hallock, 53, lost her home to fire for a second time in less than a decade. She moved into the rebuilt house in 2019, a year after an electrical fire burned it down. On Saturday, with a giant plume of smoke and flames visible on the nearby mountaintop, she fled with her children, grandchildren and pets. Her ex-husband tried to save the property and her vintage Cadillac, grabbing a garden hose as flames melted children’s toys and burned bushes. She urged him over the phone to get out and feared the worst when the line went dead. “He was saying he can’t breathe, it’s so dark I can’t see, and I’m screaming at him, ‘Leave the car, just leave it,’” she said Monday. Thirty minutes later, he called to say he had gotten out with the car. “I’m truly blessed because I have a place to stay with my animals and my grandkids. We were all able to get out safely,” she said from a niece’s apartment in Reno. Nevada fire spread quickly in foothills Many residents had little time to evacuate after the fire exploded in size. “Honestly, I thought it was like in a movie,” said Ruby Delatorre, who got back from a concert only to find her home in the evacuation zone. She returned Sunday to walk to her house and get a few more possessions. “I literally want to cry and go back for all my stuff. I just got what I thought I needed,” Delatorre said. Some who spotted the smoke on Saturday thought it was from another wildfire that has been burning the past two weeks. “The flames were pretty close to my house, and the smoke was really thick, but we have no idea if our house survived or not,” Jon Hanbury said Monday at Reno’s convention center, which is now a shelter. Wildfire threat remains high in the West Much of Nevada’s western edge is under an increased risk of wildfires this week because of high winds and low relative humidity, the National Interagency Fire Center said. The National Weather Service says the region will see warm, dry and breezy conditions, and that critical fire weather conditions are possible in the week’s later half. Reno sits at an elevation of 4,500 feet. Extremely dry conditions across the American West have sparked a rash of wildfires this summer. Fires in eastern Washington state forced the evacuation of 60,000 people in the Spokane area in early August. Nationwide, there have been more than 50,000 wildfires — the most over the past 10 years covering the same time period, according to the national fire center.

articles.title: Jade Gas submits TTCBM development plan in Mongolia
articles.summary: The proposed licence area includes Red Lake and the prospective Vista and Brownhill resource areas within the TTCBM project.
articles.body:
Jade Gas has lodged a plan for development of operations (PDO) for its Tavan Tolgoi Coal Bed Methane (TTCBM) project with Mongolia's regulator and agreed a proposed 502km² production licence area.

The plan for the coal bed methane project has been submitted to the Mongolian Minerals Reserve Council for approval. It sets out a framework for drilling, dewatering, gas production and long-term management of field operations.

Jade Gas said approval of the PDO would be a regulatory milestone towards securing the long-term production rights required to commercially develop the project.

In parallel, the company agreed the proposed production licence area with the Mongolian regulator. The 502km² area is roughly 80% of the existing 629km² exploration area.

The proposed area covers the Red Lake development, which contains Jade Gas' maiden coal bed methane reserves and is the initial focus of development activities.

It also covers the Vista and Brownhill areas, where Jade Gas has identified potential for further resource development.

The granting of the production licence would move TTCBM from an exploration and appraisal asset to long-term commercial development, the company said. It would provide Jade Gas with the tenure and rights required to develop, produce and monetise its gas resources.

Jade Gas said the certification of its maiden reserves, the PDO submission and the agreement on the licence area demonstrate progress on regulatory and in-country requirements for the TTCBM project.

The developments were not prerequisites or conditions precedent to the company's non-binding collaboration agreement, announced last month, progressing to a binding form.

Jade Gas executive director Joe Burke said: "The submission of the PDO, following the recent certification of our maiden CBM [coal bed methane] reserves, represents another major step in transitioning TTCBM from exploration and appraisal towards long-term commercial development."

TTCBM is located in the production sharing agreement area of the Tavantolgoi XXXIII unconventional gas basin.

Jade Gas operates and manages the project through Methane Gas Resource, a joint venture company with the Mongolian Government.

The Australian Securities Exchange-listed company said it transitioned from explorer to developer after the formal approval of Mongolia's first-ever natural gas reserves in June 2026.

In July, Jade Gas signed a non-binding collaboration agreement with Beijing Energy Linking and its consortium partners to secure an estimated A$1.1bn ($771m) in funding for phase one development of the Red Lake project.

"Jade Gas submits TTCBM development plan in Mongolia" was originally created and published by Offshore Technology , a GlobalData owned brand.
paragraphs: Jade Gas has lodged a plan for development of operations (PDO) for its Tavan Tolgoi Coal Bed Methane (TTCBM) project with Mongolia's regulator and agreed a proposed 502km² production licence area.

The plan for the coal bed methane project has been submitted to the Mongolian Minerals Reserve Council for approval. It sets out a framework for drilling, dewatering, gas production and long-term management of field operations.
Jade Gas said approval of the PDO would be a regulatory milestone towards securing the long-term production rights required to commercially develop the project.
In parallel, the company agreed the proposed production licence area with the Mongolian regulator. The 502km² area is roughly 80% of the existing 629km² exploration area.
The proposed area covers the Red Lake development, which contains Jade Gas' maiden coal bed methane reserves and is the initial focus of development activities.
It also covers the Vista and Brownhill areas, where Jade Gas has identified potential for further resource development.

The granting of the production licence would move TTCBM from an exploration and appraisal asset to long-term commercial development, the company said. It would provide Jade Gas with the tenure and rights required to develop, produce and monetise its gas resources.
Jade Gas said the certification of its maiden reserves, the PDO submission and the agreement on the licence area demonstrate progress on regulatory and in-country requirements for the TTCBM project.
The developments were not prerequisites or conditions precedent to the company's non-binding collaboration agreement, announced last month, progressing to a binding form.

Jade Gas executive director Joe Burke said: "The submission of the PDO, following the recent certification of our maiden CBM [coal bed methane] reserves, represents another major step in transitioning TTCBM from exploration and appraisal towards long-term commercial development."
TTCBM is located in the production sharing agreement area of the Tavantolgoi XXXIII unconventional gas basin.
Jade Gas operates and manages the project through Methane Gas Resource, a joint venture company with the Mongolian Government.
The Australian Securities Exchange-listed company said it transitioned from explorer to developer after the formal approval of Mongolia's first-ever natural gas reserves in June 2026.

articles.title: Can AMD (AMD) Win From the Shift Toward More CPU-Heavy AI Data Centers?
articles.summary: Guinness Global Innovators, an investment management company, recently released its Q2 2026 quarterly investor update for its “Guinness Global Innovators Fun...
articles.body:
Guinness Global Innovators, an investment management company, recently released its Q2 2026 quarterly investor update for its "Guinness Global Innovators Fund". You can download the letter here . The Guinness Global Innovators Fund focuses on investing in global companies that benefit from innovation in technology, communication, globalization, and management strategies. In the second quarter of 2026, the Guinness Global Innovators Fund returned 13.8% in GBP, compared with 13.0% for the MSCI World Index and 13.1% for the IA Global sector average. Easing Middle East tensions, falling oil prices, and renewed enthusiasm for artificial intelligence helped reverse much of the caution seen earlier in the year, with investors rotating back toward growth stocks and AI infrastructure beneficiaries. The Fund benefited from its overweight position in the Information Technology sector, while its overweight position in Communication Services detracted. Avoiding weaker Utilities, Materials, and Energy also supported relative performance. Also, please check the Fund's top five holdings to see its best picks for 2026.

In its second-quarter 2026 investor letter, Guinness Global Innovators Fund highlighted Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ: AMD ) as a new holding. Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMD) is a leading semiconductor company that designs and manufactures AI accelerators, microprocessors, and graphics processing units. On August 21, 2026, Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMD) closed at $473.25 per share, reflecting a market capitalization of $772.57 billion. Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMD) posted a one-month return of -4.38%, while its shares gained 189.70% over the past 52 weeks.

Guinness Global Innovators Fund stated the following regarding Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMD) in its Q2 2026 investor letter:

" Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMD) is a fabless semiconductor company focused on high-performance and AI computing. It designs and sells a broad portfolio of AI-optimised processors and networking chips, positioning itself as a full-stack solutions provider across cloud and AI infrastructure while maintaining strong competitive positioning in PC and gaming endmarkets. AMD has notably closed the performance gap with Nvidia in recent years, driven by targeted acquisitions and sustained software investment. The Helios platform, built on AMD's acquisition of systems integrator ZT Systems, is AMD's first rack-scale system unifying graphical processing units (GPUs), computer processing units (CPUs) and Pensando networking into a frontier AI infrastructure solution, and should be a material growth driver from 2027 onwards. AMD is also structurally advantaged by a shift in data centre computational architecture. Its EPYC server CPUs offer industryleading performance-per-dollar and have taken substantial share from Intel in enterprise and cloud deployments. The rapid build-out of AI infrastructure is driving demand for high core-density server CPUs to meet the orchestration requirements of agentic workloads, and the rise of AI agents could push the CPU-to-GPU deployment ratio toward parity, representing a four-times to eight-times increase from current levels. Beyond the data centre, AMD's edge AI and FPGA franchises represent underappreciated optionality, with meaningful exposure to inference at the edge as AI workloads migrate beyond centralised infrastructure." ( Click here to read the full text )

articles.title: Nigeria drug arrests: '101-year-old great-grandmother' detained for selling cannabis
articles.summary: Esther Ogunmabo is accused of selling "retail sachets" of a strain of cannabis known as skunk.
articles.body:
An elderly woman, who the authorities say is 101, has been arrested in Nigeria for allegedly selling cannabis, in a case that has drawn widespread attention.

Esther Ogunmabo, described as a great-grandmother, was apprehended on Saturday in Ogun state, in the south-west of the country, the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) announced.

Femi Babafemi, the agency's media director, said the centenarian was found with "retail sachets of skunk, a strain of cannabis weighing 90 grams, which she claims she sells to locals".

The NDLEA said the suspect told investigators that she turned to the illicit drug trade after her provisions shop was destroyed by fire. She has been released on bail.

According to the Ndlea, one of her daughters, who lives in Lagos, allegedly arranged for the supply of the substance to her every four days. Ogunmabo is accused of then selling it on in smaller quantities to customers in her community.

Ndlea chief executive Mohamed Marwa directed that the suspect be granted bail and given counselling because of her advanced age.

Nigeria influencer arrested after seizure of cocaine worth $28m destined for the UK

How Mexican drug cartels have outsourced meth labs to Nigeria

Ogunmabo’s bail status means she could still be charged for criminal activity.

Ogunmabo’s arrest came as the Ndlea also reported significant drug seizures along Nigeria's maritime routes.

In Akwa Ibom state, operatives acting on credible intelligence intercepted a wooden boat on the high seas last Friday, which was heading to Cameroon, and arrested three people on board.

More than 42kg of narcotics were recovered from the suspects.

In what the agency described as a milestone, the Ndlea also recorded its first-ever seizure of illicit drugs shipped from Thailand.

articles.title: Network Rail sues companies for Â£5m over Llanegennech derailment
articles.summary: More than 400,000 litres of fuel spilled in the area causing an "environmental disaster".
articles.body:
Network Rail is suing two rail companies for more than Â£5m after a fuel spill caused by a train derailment threatened an "environmental disaster" at a designated site for protection.

The body filed a legal claim earlier this month against DB Cargo UK and Touax Rail over the derailment near Llangennech, Carmarthenshire, in August 2020.

The incident saw 10 wagons of the 25-wagon train derail , causing 446,000 litres of fuel to spill, and about 300 people had to leave the area due to the blaze.

In High Court documents, Network Rail claimed that the derailment occurred because the wagon had "not been maintained with reasonable care" and is seeking damages for negligence.

No one was injured, but 116,000 litres of fuel ignited while 330,000 litres drained into surrounding wetlands, which form part of a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) and a Special Area of Conservation.

The Rail Accident Investigation Branch (RAIB) concluded in January 2022 that the derailment was caused by a set of wheels on one of the wagons locking, likely the result of a brake defect after "inadequate maintenance practices" were found in the investigation.

Network Rail, which owns, operates, maintains and develops Britain's railways, claimed that the derailment occurred because the wagon had "not been maintained with reasonable care" by Touax.

It is also seeking damages from DB Cargo UK, claiming that the latter "breached a contractual duty to ensure that reasonable care was taken" in maintaining the wagon.

Lawyers for the body said it expected to recover "more than Â£5m" with DB Cargo and Touax yet to file defences.

A hearing in the case is due to take place.

The locomotive was pulling the wagons from Milford Haven, Pembrokeshire, to Theale, near Reading, when the derailment occurred.

The line was closed for six months after the incident and did not fully reopen for almost a year, with 30,000 tonnes of fuel-soaked soil having to be excavated.

Bill Kelly, the then-Network Rail Wales route director, said when the line fully reopened in March 2021 that work following the incident was "one of the biggest environmental recovery operations Network Rail has ever been involved with".

He added that the derailment could have caused a "total environmental disaster".

The RAIB said, in its 2022 report, that the train was travelling at about 38mph at the time of the derailment, and was carrying up to 75.5 tonnes of fuel.

The RAIB did not establish blame or liability for the incident, but made nine recommendations to avoid similar accidents.

Network Rail and DB Cargo declined to comment, while Touax has been approached for comment.

articles.title: Police pass Mohamed Al Fayed case file to prosecutors
articles.summary: The Crown Prosecution Service will review evidence relating to a man in his 80s gathered by police investigating allegations against the late Harrods owner.
articles.body:
The Metropolitan Police have sent a file of evidence to the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) relating to a man in his 80s as part of its investigation into claims of sexual assault against Mohamed Al Fayed.

A man and a woman, both in their 80s, were interviewed under caution last month on suspicion of aiding and abetting rape and sexual assault, and assisting the commission of sexual offences.

The CPS will now decide whether a charge can be made.

Earlier this year, three women, aged in their 40s, 50s and 60s, and one man in his 60s were also questioned. The former Harrods owner died three years ago aged 94 having never faced any charges.

Al Fayed was accused by more than 20 women of sexual assault in a BBC document and podcast that aired in September 2024.

Since those allegations more than 400 alleged victims or witnesses have come forward to lawyers .

A Met Police spokesperson said "detectives submitted a full evidential file" to the CPS for a "charging decision".

"The file relates to one suspect, a man in his 80s, and relates to two indecent assaults on two women in London. Officers will continue to work closely with CPS prosecutors as the case progresses.

"To date, seven suspects have been interviewed under caution on suspicion of offences including aiding and abetting rape and sexual assault, assisting in the commission of sexual offences, and human trafficking for the purposes of sexual exploitation."

Co-chairs of the Justice for Fayed and Harrods Survivors, Jen Mills and Lindsay Mason, welcomed the latest development.

"The submission of a full evidential file to the CPS is a significant step, and it matters most of all for the two women whose allegations are at the centre of it," the statement said.

"Both are members of Justice for Fayed and Harrods Survivors and, as with all those impacted by this scandal, we stand alongside them with love and empathy."

A spokesperson from another Fayed survivor group, No One Above, said: "We call on the Met to confirm it is securing evidence on all perpetrators and co-conspirators - including the financial and documentary evidence of how victims were recruited, screened, moved, harboured and silenced."

Harrods - which was sold by Al Fayed in 2010 - previously told the BBC it was in the process of settling more than 250 claims for compensation .

articles.title: US set for largest mass visa revocation in history targeting up to 200,000 foreigners, officials say
articles.summary: The Trump administration is preparing to revoke the business and tourism visas of up to 200,000 foreigners who have applied for or are currently seeking asyl...
articles.body:
WASHINGTON (AP) — The Trump administration is preparing to revoke the business and tourism visas of up to 200,000 foreigners who have applied for or are currently seeking asylum status in the United States. If it happens, the move would be the largest single mass revocation of visas in U.S. history and would likely face legal challenges.

Unless challenged or revised, the State Department is expected to announce in the coming weeks the revocation of so-called B1 and B2 visas issued between 2016 and 2026 whose holders have sought asylum or are now seeking asylum, according to State Department documents obtained by The Associated Press and two U.S. officials. The action will be taken in coordination with the Department of Homeland Security.

"We are coordinating with DHS to identify and revoke the nonimmigrant visas of foreigners who have come to the United States claiming to be short-term visitors, but then file for asylum to stay here permanently," said State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott.

He declined to comment on the number of visas that might be revoked, saying "as the process will be ongoing, the number of revocations remains dynamic and will be done on a rolling basis."

The revocations would not necessarily result in their immediate deportation, the officials said. Most of those with asylum cases currently pending would be recategorized but would lose their status as business or tourism travelers, according to the officials, who spoke on condition of anonymity because the revocations are not final yet.

Since President Donald Trump took office for his second term last year, his administration has steadily ramped up restrictions on visa applicants — demanding more information about their social media histories, requiring the posting of expensive bonds for the processing of visas, and outright banning the issuance of visas to citizens of certain countries.

In a social media post on Monday, Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau called out people who he said try to use tourist and business visas to get into the United States and then apply for asylum.

"People in the US and all over the world are fed up with bogus asylum claims," Landau wrote on X. "Asylum isn't supposed to be a loophole to circumvent immigration law." Landau cited the case of a Colombian citizen who came to the U.S. in 2015 on a tourist visa and then applied for asylum.

B1 visas are generally issued for business trips and B2 visas are generally issued for tourism, family visits or medical care. It was not immediately clear from the documents or the officials how many of these visa holders are seeking or have sought asylum in the United States and would be affected by the revocations.

Current applicants for B1 and B2 visas are asked to affirm that they will not apply for asylum in the United States and prove that they intend to return to their home countries.

In the past 18 months, the State Department has revoked about 175,000 visas for people who have been convicted or accused of crimes ranging from drunken driving to rape and robbery, as well as for people who have spoken out publicly against U.S. policies, particularly in the Middle East.

The administration has also moved to crack down on so-called birth tourism, a practice the administration claims is used by foreign pregnant women to come to the United States to give birth so that their child will benefit from birthright citizenship . Trump has tried several times to end birthright citizenship, but those challenges have been rejected by courts, including the Supreme Court.

The State Department documents obtained by the AP suggest screening of current B1 and B2 visa holders began after the State Department received information about asylum requests from the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services.

articles.title: U.S. removes Syria from terrorism sponsor list, lifting major investment obstacle
articles.summary: Monday’s announcement also delisted the Nusrah Front as a terrorist group, leaving Cuba, Iran and North Korea as the three countries Washington designates as state sponsors of terrorism.
articles.body: The United States removed Syria from its list of state sponsors of terrorism on Monday, lifting what Damascus says was the last major impediment to investing in the country as Washington deepens ties to the new Syrian government. The removal, posted on the U.S. Treasury’s website, took effect after a 45-day congressional review period triggered when President Donald Trump formally notified Congress on July 8 of his intention to rescind the designation. “These actions were all taken in recognition of the positive actions taken and further commitments by the Syrian government under President Ahmed al-Sharaa to fully distance Syria from acts of international terrorism,” U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in a statement. Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shibani told Reuters on Saturday that the government hoped removing what he called the “last obstacle” would help reconnect Syria to the global financial and economic system and boost investment. “There is no longer any obstacle to investment, doing business and rebuilding economic life in Syria,” he said. Syria had been on the list since 1979, when Washington accused the government of former President Hafez al-Assad of supporting militant groups. The designation remained throughout the rule of his son Bashar al-Assad, who was toppled by rebels led by current President Ahmed al-Sharaa in December 2024. Cuba, Iran, North Korea remain Monday’s announcement also removed the designation of the Nusrah Front as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist organization, leaving Cuba, Iran and North Korea as the three countries designated by Washington as state sponsors of terrorism. The designation carries restrictions on U.S. foreign assistance, defense exports and sales, certain dual-use items and financial transactions, and had remained a major deterrent for banks and investors even after Washington dismantled its broader sanctions program on Syria. Trump’s administration terminated comprehensive U.S. sanctions on Syria in July 2025, while maintaining targeted sanctions against Assad and his associates, rights abusers, drug traffickers, Islamic State and al Qaeda affiliates and Iranian proxies. The U.S. Treasury has since said American financial institutions can provide services to Syria, process payments involving Syrian banks and establish correspondent banking relationships with them, provided sanctioned parties are not involved. But the terrorism designation remained a source of legal and compliance risk for firms considering entering Syria, whose government is seeking billions of dollars in investment to rebuild after nearly 14 years of war. Signs of interest had grown ahead of the removal. articles.title: ‘Getting no help’: Thousands in Gary, Indiana, still without power nearly 2 weeks after storms
articles.summary: For some in the predominantly Black city, the lack of electricity has caused medical complications, while others are cooking what food they can at local parks before it spoils.
articles.body: GARY, Ind. — The power outages caused by storms that roared through the region nearly two weeks ago have one resident of this Rust Belt city literally gasping for air. Joetta Walker, who is 73 and has asthma, uses a nebulizer to help her breathe. But right now it’s a useless piece of machinery, and she has had to rely on an inhaler to survive. “I have a nebulizer where I need to take breathing treatments,” Walker said in an interview at her sweltering home. “I can’t do that without the electricity.” Walker said the inhaler doesn’t give her the same level of relief. “I wheeze,” Walker said and demonstrated. “You hear it now because I get too hot.” No other place in Indiana has suffered more as a result of those Aug. 11 storms than this mostly Black city on the southern tip of Lake Michigan, best known as the hometown of Michael Jackson and the Jackson 5. As of Monday, more than 8,600 customers were still waiting for their power to be restored, most of them in Gary, the Northern Indiana Public Service Co. (NIPSCO) reported on its website. Mayor Eddie Melton said he spoke with President Donald Trump and told him “explicitly that we needed help, that we needed resources.” Melton said he asked Trump to sign an executive order “and move this thing forward so folks can start getting back to work and we start restoring Gary back to normal.” “He said that he was going to do all that he can,” Melton said. Melton said he also met with Republican Sen. Jim Banks. He hopes power for residents will be fully restored by Tuesday. “I believe a good chunk of that will be restored today, and hopefully 100% will be restored tomorrow,” he said. Melton’s hopeful forecast came a day after he ripped NIPSCO for failing to completely restore electricity to his city. “Twelve days is too long for families to be without power,” he said Sunday in an address posted on the city’s Facebook page. “I have made it clear the current pace of restoration is unacceptable.” In an email Monday, NIPSCO, the Merrillville, Indiana-based utility provider that supplies natural gas and electricity to over 1.3 million residential and commercial customers across the northern third of the state, said it’s “focused on safely restoring power to all customers in every affected community.” On its website, it said it expects to restore power to all of its customers in Gary by Tuesday. Walker said that can’t happen too soon. She said she has been relying on her nieces to bring her food and charge up her cellphone twice a day. She said she has $750 worth of pork chops, spiral hams and other foods rotting in her nonfunctioning freezer and refrigerator. “All gone, gone,” she said. At night, Walker said, she gets around the house by candlelight. “I feel hurt ... because I feel like they can do better than this,” she said of the power company. “But I also understand how much damage was done, and I also understand the workers have to be tired.” Another Gary resident, Dion Thomas, 40, said Monday was the first time he’d seen power crews in his neighborhood. But they seemed to be struggling to turn the electricity back on. “Some people’s stuff was coming on, then it went back out,” he said. In the meantime, people have been heading to parks to cook whatever food they have left over charcoal and eat it before it spoils, said Thomas, a father of three. “It’s been crazy,” he said. Since the power went out, there has been a spate of generator thefts in his neighborhood, said Calvin Boone, 44, a father of four. “The kids running around, they stealing people’s generators right now,” Boone said. “I think about the older people, the health for them.” Boone said that everybody has been feeling hot and miserable and that some have taken to sleeping in their cars with the engines on and the air conditioners blasting. “We ain’t getting no help,” he said. Channie Weaver got her power back overnight. But it was too late to save the food in her fridge. She said she’d gone shopping right before the storms hit and estimates she lost $300 worth of provisions. “All the food is gone. We about to go out and get something out to eat,” said Weaver, 50. Weaver said she lives with her 22-year-old daughter, Desaray Weaver, and her granddaughters, Raelynn, 2, and Riley, 1. “Man, it’s been rough,” Weaver said. “Being hot in the house, no air conditioning, plus my daughter — she’s pregnant. But it’s definitely been rough.” Weaver and other Gary residents said in interviews that they can’t help but wonder whether the reason their city’s power is getting restored last is that it’s a mostly Black city. “I feel like we at the bottom before everybody else,” she said. Shaquille Brewster and Selina Guevara reported from Gary and Corky Siemaszko from New York City.

articles.title: âMust correct its toneâ: Iranâs Pezeshkian warns US against âcoercion and bullyingâ in Munir meet
articles.summary: Middle East News: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has told Pakistan Army chief Asim Munir that the United States must change its approach towards Tehran, warning th.
articles.body: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has told Pakistan Army chief Asim Munir that the United States must change its approach towards Tehran, warning that âcoercion and bullyingâ would complicate diplomatic efforts.Pezeshkian made the remarks during a meeting with Munir in Tehran on Monday, according to the official website of the Iranian President.Munir arrived in Iran for talks with Iranian officials amid heightened regional tensions and continuing friction between Tehran and Washington.The Iranian president also expressed hope that continued cooperation between Iran and Pakistan would help achieve the goals outlined in a 14-point Memorandum of Understanding (MoU).âThe United States must correct its tone and approach in its interactions with Iran, because relying on coercion and bullying will only complicate the implementation processes,â Pezeshkian said.He stressed that Washington should adhere to its commitments to Iran based on international law and standards.Pezeshkian also said Iran would withstand pressure by relying on national solidarity.âOur nation will overcome any pressure and threat by relying on this solidarity,â he said.Pezeshkian stresses regional cooperation, unityDuring the meeting, Pezeshkian stressed the need for lasting peace and security in the region and called for greater cooperation with Islamic countries and neighbouring states.âThe Islamic Republic of Iran is ready for any cooperation and interaction in the economic, political, and security dimensions with Islamic countries and neighbours, because the Holy Prophet (PBUH) has always commanded peace and friendship,â he said.He also emphasised the importance of unity among Islamic countries, describing it as a deterrent against what he called the âconspiracies of the Zionist regime and the enemies of Islamâ.âThe unity and cohesion of Islamic countries is the most important deterrent against the conspiracies of the Zionist regime and the enemies of Islam, and if this convergence is realised, the enemies will not be able to advance their sinister goals,â Pezeshkian said.The Iranian president also referred to coordination within Iran to advance regional peace and stability and expressed hope that Pakistan's diplomatic efforts would contribute to stability in the region.He said he hoped the âIslamic world will achieve increasing growth, dignity, and prideâ.Munir, in turn, thanked Pezeshkian for his efforts towards establishing regional stability and peace.âIn order to advance common goals and achieve a comprehensive agreement, it is essential that diplomatic processes be discussed and examined with complete precision and meticulousness,â Munir said, according to the Iranian president's official website.The Pakistan Army chief also welcomed the growing trend of bilateral cooperation between the two countries.He said the âdeep historical, religious and cultural commonalities between Pakistan and Iran are a valuable asset for overcoming the current complex circumstances and charting a bright futureâ.Munirâs Iran visit follows Trump callMunir's visit to Tehran comes after he spoke by phone with US President Donald Trump last week, according to US media reports. A source familiar with the conversation told CNN that Trump and Munir discussed Iran.Munir also met Iranian officials during his visit. Iran's state broadcaster IRIB reported that he held talks with Major General Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council.Rezaei also called on Washington to change its behaviour and take practical steps to implement the 14-point MoU.Earlier on Monday, Iranian Parliamentary Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf also met Munir in Tehran. According to a statement shared by Ghalibaf on Telegram, the two discussed what Iran described as repeated US breaches of commitments under the MoU.âThe commitments of the parties in the Memorandum of Understanding are clear, and it was America that, by breaching its commitments, prevented the establishment of stability in the region and created another reason for distrust in this country,â Ghalibaf said.He said Tehran remained committed to implementing the MoU and that Iran would not be affected by external pressure.âWe are pursuing the implementation of the terms of the Memorandum of Understanding, and it is America that must adhere to its commitments based on the Memorandum of Understanding,â the statement quoted him as saying.Munir also said he would continue his efforts to restore stability in the region, according to the statement.Iran faces fresh US economic pressureMunir's visit comes as Washington has announced fresh economic sanctions against Iran.US treasury secretary Scott Bessent on Monday unveiled new measures targeting 60 individuals, entities and vessels, while stopping short of imposing the most severe penalties threatened against countries that continue trading with Iran.Iranian economy minister Ali Madanizadeh said Tehran was prepared to respond to the new sanctions.âWe are fully prepared for the US sanctions,â Madanizadeh said, according to Reuters.He said Iran had its own tools to respond to what he described as an economic attack and claimed that China and Russia had not accepted the US measures.Pakistan's earlier mediation efforts between Washington and Tehran had resulted in an interim peace agreement signed in June, but the Islamabad Memorandum subsequently faltered.Against this backdrop, Munir's meetings with Iran's top political and security officials have focused on diplomatic processes, regional stability and implementation of the 14-point MoU.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
